means:
Able to turn your hand to many different things — and be **good** at all of them. Also used of objects: a tool or material with many uses.

The praise is about **range plus competence**, which is what separates it from its neighbours. *Adaptable* means you cope when conditions change; *flexible* means you bend to others' demands; **versatile** means you already have several skills sitting ready. It's a compliment nobody objects to — an actor who does comedy and Chekhov, a fabric that works in summer and winter.
trap: ⚠️ **versatile ≠ volatile.** Same rhythm, opposite temperament: **versatile** = usefully many-sided; **volatile** = liable to explode or swing wildly.
trick_line: Hiding in it is **versa** — as in *vice versa*: it turns the other way, and any other way you need.
trick_unpack: The versatile one keeps turning to face a new task and lands each one well.
sentences: A **versatile** performer, she moved from stand-up to Shakespeare without any visible change of gear.
Get the black one — it's the most **versatile** jacket you own; it goes with everything.
in_the_wild: Sports commentary lives on this word: the cricketing **all-rounder** who bats, bowls and keeps, or the footballer who can fill in at three positions, is always called "the most versatile player in the squad."
etymology: Latin **vertere** = *"to turn"* → *versatilis*, "capable of turning." The same root turns up everywhere on the GRE: **convert, invert, divert, avert, revert, adverse, vertigo**, and **anniversary** (the year turning round again).
one_line: Skilled at many different things; useful in many ways.
